Exercise 1. a) About two million people need humanitarian aid. · b) One in five children suffer from acute malnutrition. · c) The city's only water plant has been damaged. · d) Thousands of families have taken refuge in schools and reception centres. · e) Humanitarian access to mountain areas is still limited. · f) The reconstruction started slowly. Exercise 6. 1. The United Nations has launched an urgent appeal to collect 500 Millions of dollars. · 2. Donors committed to the conference 300 millions. · 3. The appeal has been funded only to 20%. · 4. The programme was forced to reduce food rations due to lack of funds. · 5. An international organisation has suspended its activities in the area for security reasons. Exercise 7. a) host communities · b) the most vulnerable groups · c) voluntary return · d) emergency relief · e) essential needs · f) cash aid (monetary transfers) Exercise 8. a) It is estimated that the number of displaced persons is one hundred thousand. b) Donors have pledged to pay a billion dollars. c) The agency warned of the risk of famine. d) Hundreds of migrants have arrived on the coast (legal status is unknown). · e) A human rights organisation has accused the army of committing war crimes. 9. a) Table: approx. 30 000 (estimate, OCHA, last week's report); internally displaced persons 70 000 (estimate, same source); refugees about 15 000 in the neighbouring country (registration, UNHCR); half of the population in severe food insecurity (OCHA, same ratio); appeal 200 million dollars for six months, funded by 25% (UN); Donor promises largely not yet arrived (last month's conference). They do not add up because they measure different groups (reentered, still displaced, refugees abroad), with different methods (estimate, registration) and perhaps with overlaps. Needs: damaged homes, out-of-service water and electricity networks, closed schools, food insecurity, risk of epidemics in overcrowded camps. Access: some unsafe mountain roads, convoys that take days to pass the checkpoints. b) This is the regional director of the programme, on behalf of the programme. Reduce rations to help more people or stop helping some of them altogether. Facts: reduction of rations for about half a million people in three countries; received only on 40% the necessary funds; reduction of a third from next month. Declarations: the words of the director. Forecast: the cut could be ⁧قد⁩ , step 3) increase malnutrition. Requests: that donors honour commitments and provide flexible and multi-annual funds. The ⁧إما⁩ … ⁧وإما⁩ ... is not a false misleading dilemma: it describes a real choice imposed by the lack of funds, even if presented in a dramatic way; an analyst may note that there are also other options (more funds), which are precisely the object of the appeal. Exercise 10. 1. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs estimates that about three million people need humanitarian aid, including one million children. 2. Since the beginning of the crisis, UNHCR has registered more than two hundred thousand refugees in neighbouring countries, while the number of internally displaced persons is estimated at twice as much.

3. The World Health Organization warned against the risk of cholera spreading due to the damage to water and sewerage systems. 4. An international human rights organisation has accused the conflicting parties of ... serious violations of international humanitarian law ... , requesting the establishment of an independent commission of inquiry. 5. The humanitarian appeal has so far been funded only by the 30%, despite the commitments made by donors at last spring's conference. Delicate points: in 1 ⁧يقدر⁩ • estimate • • in 2 separate registration and estimation; in 4 quotation marks and attribution; in 5 ⁧تعهدات⁩ (i) commitments (not liabilities) Exercise 11. Personal answer. The tutor controls: real institutional text with links and dates; names of the organisation in Arabic and English; each digit with type and source; technical or legal terms attributed to those who use them; no information added from other sources; neutral Arabic summary. Exercise 12. a) Because it is a technical term, which is used when a competent body declares it according to precise criteria; the site used it improperly or generically. Severe food insecurity for about half the population and risk of famine in some areas. The estimate is an approximate assessment; The census is a count. Because there are real people behind the words. b) It has put "refugee, displaced, migrant" as synonyms. Refugee: crossed the border and enjoys international protection according to a legal definition; internally displaced: he left the house but remained in his country; asylum seeker: has requested protection and awaits the decision; migrant: generic term for those who move from one country to another for any reason. The competent authorities, not the translator. c) About 40 000 people in need (estimate); A convoy of twenty trucks with food and medicine arrived yesterday in the mountain area, the first time in three months. Registered refugees in the neighbouring country, over 20 000 (registration). That the fields have reached maximum capacity.
